response: Alveolar macrophage phagocytic dysfunction in children with protracted bacterial bronchitis may contribute to neutrophilic inflammation and bacterial colonization, which are also characteristics of bronchiectasis. However, it is currently unknown whether this mechanism specifically contributes to the progression of protracted bacterial bronchitis to bronchiectasis. In other words, while there is a potential link between alveolar macrophage phagocytic dysfunction and the development of bronchiectasis, more research is needed to confirm this relationship.
